_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 3 Mathematics unit lecture film, Lesson 5 Shapes and Symmetry. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow the lesson's own steps in order - Naming flat shapes, Regular or irregular, Lines of symmetry, Mirror it, Solid shapes, All the way round and Counting the space inside - and use the lesson's own numbers: a square standing on its corner is still a square, a square has four lines of symmetry and a rectangle two, a reflection lands the same distance the other side, a cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners with 3 edges hidden, and the 6 cm by 2 cm rectangle has a perimeter of 16 cm and covers 12 squares (both figures are the lesson's own, from its How do you know bank and its check).
title: Shapes and Symmetry
subtitle: Grade 3 Mathematics
objectives: Identify, describe, classify, name and sketch 2D shapes by their properties. Differentiate between regular and irregular polygons.
Understand that perimeter is the total distance around a 2D shape and can be calculated by adding lengths, and area is how much space a 2D shape occupies within its boundary.
Draw lines, rectangles and squares. Estimate, measure and calculate the perimeter of a shape, using appropriate metric units, and area on a square grid.
Identify, describe, sort, name and sketch 3D shapes by their properties.
Recognise pictures, drawings and diagrams of 3D shapes.
Identify both horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry on 2D shapes and patterns.
Sketch the reflection of a 2D shape in a horizontal or vertical mirror line, including where the mirror line is the edge of the shape.

beats.say: Every flat shape has a name, and the sides tell you which.
Shapes fold in half, flip over a mirror, and have a distance round the edge.
A flat shape is named by how many straight sides it has.
Three straight sides and three corners. That is a triangle.
Four straight sides make a quadrilateral. A square is one.
Five sides is a pentagon. Six sides is a hexagon.
Stand a square on its corner. It is still a square, not a diamond.

at.stand: Stand a square on its corner

beats.say: Regular means every side is the same length, and every corner too.
Both of these have five sides, so both of them are pentagons.
Only one of them is regular. The other is stretched.

at.one: Only one of them is regular

beats.say: Irregular is not wrong. Most shapes around you are irregular.
A line of symmetry is a fold line, drawn on the shape.
Fold along it, and the two halves land on top of each other.
Count them with me. A square has four lines of symmetry.
A rectangle has only two: down the middle, and across.
Cutting a shape in two is not enough. The halves must match.
A reflection flips a shape over a mirror line.
Every square lands the same distance on the other side.
This square is two along. Its reflection is two along as well.
Four squares on this side, so four squares on that side.
A reflection is not a slide. It turns the shape round.
A solid shape is not flat. This one is a cube.
A face is a flat surface. A cube has six faces.
An edge is where two faces meet. A cube has twelve edges.
A corner is where edges meet. A cube has eight corners.
The drawing is flat. Three edges hide round the back. Count those too.
Perimeter is the whole distance round the outside edge.
This rectangle is six centimetres by two centimetres.
Only two numbers are written on it. The other two sides match.
Six plus two plus six plus two makes sixteen centimetres.

at.sum: Six plus two plus six plus two

beats.say: Area is different. It is the space inside, counted in squares.
Twelve squares inside, and sixteen centimetres round the edge.
Count the sides to name a flat shape. Regular means every side the same.
A line of symmetry folds a shape onto itself. A reflection flips it.
A cube has six faces, twelve edges and eight corners.
Perimeter goes round the edge. Area is the space inside.
